Bug_Details: Calling Iterator.hasNext() is not supposed to have any side effects and hence should not change the iterator’s state. Iterator.next() advances the iterator by one item. So calling it inside Iterator.hasNext() breaks the hasNext() contract and will lead to unexpected behavior in production.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is in the use of `hasNext` method in `while` loop. This method is supposed to return true if there are more elements in the iteration, but it also advances the iteration. Hence, it leads to skipping of elements in the iteration. In this case, it skips the first even number (2) and returns the first odd number (3) instead of the next odd number (1).
